claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the current model release is compliant because aggregate readiness passed and rehearsal was clean, despite a newly observed small-business onboarding weakness, on the theory that certification remains supportable if that weakness is reflected in current release documentation.
specific_concerns: The admissible record available to this role is only the actor's summary, not the underlying current release documentation or approval artifacts.

The policy requires that current release documentation reflect current evaluation results and disclose material segment weaknesses or show approved mitigation; the summary states this must occur but does not show that it has occurred.
The small-business onboarding weakness appears unresolved and is tied to a named launch use case, creating an unresolved policy predicate on materiality/disclosure.
Prior approval and informal monitoring are expressly contextual only under the policy and cannot carry the certification decision.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant, rather than only potentially supportable after documentation is updated or approved mitigation is shown.
That the current release documentation already reflects the present subgroup weakness.
That no approved mitigation is needed because disclosure has already been completed or the weakness is not material.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release model card or release documentation showing the small-business onboarding weakness is explicitly disclosed with current evaluation results.
Provide any approved mitigation or risk-acceptance record if certification is relying on mitigation instead of disclosure alone.
Provide the underlying current-release evaluation artifact establishing the aggregate pass, the subgroup gap, and the relevance of that subgroup to named launch use cases.
Provide the release-governance record showing the certification decision reviewed the current regression rather than relying on prior approval context.
decision_criteria: If current release documentation already includes the current evaluation results and clearly discloses the small-business onboarding weakness, the verdict could improve toward compliant_with_caveats or compliant.
If an approved mitigation/risk acceptance exists covering the current subgroup weakness, that would satisfy the missing policy link.
If underlying evidence shows the subgroup is not a material segment weakness for a named launch use case, the compliance concern would weaken.
Absent proof of current documentation or approved mitigation, policy does not support a clean compliance finding.
